description: CA exposes an HTTP web-enrollment endpoint without EPA; coerce a privileged account and NTLM-relay it to enroll.

telemetry.detail: Authentication coercion (PetitPotam/PrinterBug/etc.) generates distinctive MS-EFSR/MS-RPRN RPC traffic to the victim.
Relayed NTLM authentication lands as a logon on the CA/web endpoint.
Certificate Services received a certificate request (on the CA).
Certificate Services issued a certificate (on the CA).
PKINIT TGT request using the issued certificate - certificate-logon anomaly.
Coercion-plus-relay chains are heavily signatured; NTLM relay to ADCS web enrollment is a well-known, widely-detected pattern.

prerequisite_privilege: Network position to coerce a target and relay to the CA web endpoint (no directory rights needed)
abuse_primitive: Coerce a DC/computer account, relay to /certsrv, obtain a machine/DA-capable cert.
notes: Loudest of the ESC set: it combines coercion RPC traffic, a relayed logon, and CA issuance. Network-side detections are mature. Requires the vulnerable HTTP endpoint.
